solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sympathetic behaviour principally seen in bearded men, curiously

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters that come before it are rearranged
principally means mainly or at the start, so only the opening letter of seen is used

explanation.surface: Somebody notices that men with beards behave in an oddly sympathetic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges S, IN and BEARDEDMEN together; 'principally' takes the first letter of 'seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a doctor's tactful, reassuring way with a patient, hence kindly conduct generally.

clue.text: Finance business in Belgium earned a huge cut, mostly in error

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

indicators.note: in error means mistakenly, so the letters are put into a new order
mostly means nearly all, so the last letter of huge cut is dropped

explanation.surface: A Belgian firm made a big profit, but most of it was cut off by a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the T of HUGECUT; 'in error' rearranges EARNED, A and HUGECU behind B.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a booth or office where travellers swap one currency for another, a kind of money trade.

clue.text: Lifeless, occasionally dour, dirty place

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of dour is used

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, the classic filthy place

explanation.surface: A description of something dull, now and then grim, a filthy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes D and U, the first and third letters of 'dour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dry and stale, such as a dusty old lecture, lacks life or interest.

clue.text: Anger from one clergyman given unopened summons

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a citation is an official summons to appear in court

explanation.surface: A priest is furious after receiving a court summons he never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes the C from CITATION; RR is the abbreviation for Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance or vexation is a mild form of wrath.

clue.text: Small holes allowed to penetrate parts of potatoes

indicators.note: to penetrate means to go into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the eyes of a potato are the buds on its skin
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Little holes are permitted to pierce bits of spuds.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small reinforced holes in cloth or leather for laces or cords.

clue.text: Bullock, for example, about to be held by a lock

indicators.note: to be held by means to be contained within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
C, for circa, is the Latin abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A young bull approaches and gets tangled in a lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Bullock looks like a young bull, but it is Sandra Bullock, the Hollywood film star; 'to be held by' puts C inside A TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra Bullock is a film star, a female performer on screen.

clue.text: Last bits of production to get redone and set to music

indicators.note: last bits of means the final letters of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: The final stages of a show must be reworked and given a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last bits of' takes N, O, T and E from the ends of four words; the definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to write down a tune in musical notation, an older sense of scoring a piece.

clue.text: Body of soldiers behind a drug bust

parts.note: rear means the back or behind

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops are behind a narcotics raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a police raid but rearranges A DRUG into GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the troop unit protecting an army's back as it moves.

clue.text: Removes legal stipulations represented in disclaimers covering term of use

indicators.note: covering means going round, so the rearranged letters surround another
represented means presented again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged
term means end, so the last letter of use is taken

explanation.surface: Lawyers' disclaimers describing the terms of use drop the legal conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term of use' reads as a contract clause, but 'term' means end, giving the final E; 'represented' is the anagram signal and 'covering' wraps the result round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To legalise an activity by taking it off the list of criminal offences, lifting the legal prohibitions.

clue.text: Begrudge admitting endless desire is on the rise

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to begrudge is to resent

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Someone resents another while admitting their own boundless longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the word for desire, and 'admitting' takes it in; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rising again, reviving after a decline, is gaining strength once more.

clue.text: Time to relax, kid!

parts.note: to ease is to relax or loosen

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child it is time to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' reads as a child but is the verb to rib or josh.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to rib or joke with them playfully.

clue.text: Discontented Americans ultimately say they've got to date

indicators.note: discontented means with the contents removed, so only the outer letters of Americans remain
ultimately means finally, so the end letter of each of the three words is used

explanation.surface: Unhappy Americans eventually say they have found a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' empties Americans to AS; 'ultimately' takes Y, E and T from the ends of 'say they've got'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to now, so far.

clue.text: Tied game of rugby seeing both wings sent off

indicators.note: wings are the two flanks, so the letters at both sides are removed

parts.note: sevens is the seven-a-side form of rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby match ends level after both wingers are dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both wings sent off' strips the first and last S from SEVENS; the wings sound like rugby players but mean the word's edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A level score, with neither side ahead, is a draw.

clue.text: Jelly can go awry every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means at intervals, so alternate letters of the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: A jelly might fail to set from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and then' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of CANGOAWRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaweed extract that sets as a gel, used in cooking and in labs for growing cultures.

clue.text: Following a limited diet is terribly unfair — it primarily alters recipes

indicators.note: terribly means very badly, so the letters are put into a new order
primarily means first of all, so the opening letters of alters and recipes are used

explanation.surface: A restricted eating plan seems awfully unjust because it changes recipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives A and R; 'terribly' rearranges UNFAIR, IT, A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing someone who eats only fruit, a very restricted kind of vegetarian regime.

clue.text: Delegates situated in the outskirts of Dartford?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the letters at either end of Dartford are both D, and two of that letter spelt out are dees
put means placed or situated

explanation.surface: Representatives are based on the fringes of a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartford is a town in Kent; its two ends are D and D, spelt out as DEES, with PUT placed 'in'. The definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to hand it to someone else to do on your behalf.

clue.text: Repressed memory restricting limits of acting star

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means held in or repressed
RAM is random-access memory in a computer

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so the first and last letters of acting are used

explanation.surface: A suppressed recollection holds back a performer's range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting star' looks like a performer, but 'star' alone is the definition and 'acting' only supplies its edges via 'limits of'; 'restricting' holds them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed figure drawn with continuous lines is a star shape.

clue.text: Scornful language and right after it, audible yawning

indicators.note: after means following, so the piece for right comes behind the piece for it

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for it

indicators.note: audible means heard, so a word for yawning is given by its sound

parts.note: a chasm is a yawning gap

explanation.surface: A sneering remark, followed by noisy yawns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is crossword shorthand for sex appeal; 'after' sets right behind it; 'audible' signals a word heard rather than spelt, a yawning gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking, cutting remarks that say the opposite of what they mean are a form of derision.

clue.text: Profile clubs playing a series of games abroad?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
on means playing, as an actor on stage
a tour is a sports team's run of matches overseas

explanation.surface: A sports profile of clubs competing in a run of overseas fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline or shape of something, such as a coastline, is its profile.

clue.text: Rooms oddly chosen, very possibly where visitors crashed?

indicators.note: oddly chosen means the letters in odd positions are picked out of Rooms

parts.note: well can mean very, as in well pleased

explanation.surface: Guests, perhaps, crashed in rooms picked at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly chosen' takes R, O and S. The 'visitors' who 'crashed' sound like weary guests, but are aliens in a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in New Mexico where, legend says, a UFO came down in 1947.

clue.text: Checked the fit of extremely refined clothing that is in fashion

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: ton is an old word for style or fashion

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the outer letters surround another piece
extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of refined are used

parts.note: IE, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone checks how elegant fashionable clothing looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the ends of 'refined', 'clothing' wraps them round 'that is', and 'in' puts all of it inside a dated word for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a garment on to see whether it is the right size.

clue.text: Rule requiring rock to be stored in the mine's entrance

indicators.note: to be stored in means to be held inside, so one piece goes within another
the entrance is the way in, so the opening letter of mine's is used

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal

explanation.surface: Regulations require mined rock to be kept at the pit entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' takes the first letter of 'mine's'; 'to be stored in' puts the rock inside; 'requiring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A proven statement or principle in mathematics, a formal law.

clue.text: Healthy produce brought about some cardiac advantages

indicators.note: brought about says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eating wholesome food gives certain benefits to the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian palm berry marketed as a superfood, so a wholesome crop.

clue.text: Somewhat misleading thing I might signal

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so the letters are found within the next word

explanation.surface: A slightly deceptive signal I might send.
explanation.walkthrough: On maps the abbreviation I stands for island, so this is the land feature I can signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island, which the letter I often denotes on maps.

clue.text: Utmost efforts getting over to isolated land

indicators.note: getting over means stretching across, so one piece spans the other

parts.note: to give your all is to make the utmost effort

explanation.surface: Huge effort is needed to reach a remote place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' means spanning, so the word for utmost efforts straddles 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef or island, typically remote in the ocean.

clue.text: The final part is over. Great!

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
mega is slang for great or excellent

explanation.surface: The last part is finished, and someone cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek alphabet's last letter, used to mean the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end of anything.

clue.text: Tough person also hot in drag

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to tug is to drag or pull
H stands for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A hard man, also in a sweat while dressed in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' suggests cross-dressing but means pull; 'also' is padding that serves only as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian or hoodlum is a hard, brutal type.

clue.text: Equipment put round most of the perimeter

indicators.note: put round means turned about, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rig is equipment or gear

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

explanation.surface: Kit is placed around nearly all of the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put round' turns the gear word backwards; 'most of' trims 'the' by its last letter. 'Perimeter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement around the middle of something is its circumference.

clue.text: Queues stopping organs arriving ahead of schedule

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so one piece fills the other

parts.note: ears are organs of hearing
lines are queues

explanation.surface: Queues block body parts arriving early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' means plugging, as one stops up a hole; the definition is a noun phrase naming a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being early or prompt, coming before the expected time.

clue.text: Power-hungry people manage oil scam at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tyrants run a fraud involving offshore oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges MANAGE OIL SCAM.
explanation.definitionFit: People obsessed with power and their own importance.
